newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Terme 96 net steady, slashes dividend.
newsitem.headline: Terme 96 net steady, slashes dividend.

text.p: Slovenian health resort operator Terme Catez said on Thursday 1996 net profit firmed 0.6 percent to 367.2 million tolars ($2.35 million) but that it would slash its dividend by 120 tolars.
The company remains upbeat on the current year and expects net profit to jump some 15 percent on a 10 percent rise in sales.

The management said it proposed cutting the dividend to 300 tolars per share from 420 tolars in order to be able to invest "The dividend will be smaller because we want to invest as much as possible," chief executive Borut Mokrovic, told a news conference. The proposal still needs shareholder approval, expected in June.
Sales rose to 2.2 billion tolars from 2.1 billion in 1995.
"Our results are satisfactory considering the rainy summer last year," Mokrovic said.
Due to the bad weather, the number of one-day guests fell by 15 percent to 700,000 last year, while the number of overnight guests decreased to 432,000 from 450,000 in 1995.
Mokrovic said the company planned to expand its facilities, located on a 45 hectare (112.5 acre) site, 120 km (73 miles) south-east of Ljubljana, significantly by the year 1999.
"We will invest at least 40 million marks ($23.3 million) in the expansion of the indoor swimming area and a new hotel," Mokrovic said.
He said the investment was expected to be covered by the firm's own capital and by domestic and foreign loans.
"If it turns out that the investment calls for yet more capital, then we might consider a GDR (global depository receipt) offering abroad," Zvonko Krulc, deputy executive, told Reuters.
Terme's 1996 investment fell to $2.92 million from $3.5 million in 1995, but could jump to $17.5 million this year as a result of the expansion plans.
The number of one-day guests is expected to rise by 20 to 25 percent this year, while the number of overnight stays is seen 10 percent higher.
Currently 10 percent of guests are from abroad, mainly from Croatia, Austria, Germany and Italy, but the company expects to increase this number by introducing additional health and sport programmes.
-- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 156.36 Slovenian tolars)
